text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Interior Minister Caspar Einem may succeed Rudolf Scholten as Transport Minister, according to the newspaper. Chancellor-designate Klima plans a major reorganisation of the Social Democrat government team. Workers' chamber head Lore Hostasch might take over from Franz Hums as Social Affairs Minister. Karl Schloegl might become Interior Minister and Health Minister Christa Krammer and Women's Affairs Minister Helga Konrad are likely to step down.
- Conservative coalition partner the People's Party wants the new team to get down to work more quickly.
- Vienna's Social Democrat leader Michael Haeupl expects a change in the style of leadership.
- Austrian tax levels are towards the lower end of EU taxation.
- The EU Commission sticks to its line that anonymous savings accounts and trading accounts must be abolished.
- Industrial group Radex-Heraklith expects its profits after tax to have risen ten percent to 460 million schillings in 1996.
- The Workers' Chamber says no to the industry demands for lower taxation.
- Conservative Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel wants a say in who will become the new Finance Minister, while speculation over the People's Party leadership is growing.
- Economic research institute Wifo expects 250,000 unemployed this year.
- The Health Ministry and Social Affairs Ministry are to merged by the new Chancellor Vikto Klima, the newspaper writes.
- Wolfgang Ruttensdorfer, manager in Austria's oil company OMV, and Vienna's finance chief Rudolf Edlinger are possible candidates as Finance Minister.

- Economists and the bourse have reacted positively to the designation of Viktor Klima as new Finance Minister.
